result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers take a clear conditional position and see that the office manager's day of setup is the real cost. A goes further on qualifying prospects: it gives four concrete questions and says what to do if a prospect fails them. A also sets out pilot terms (success test, named signer, checkpoint, decision meeting) and gives a line to send to prospects, though it has some leftover placeholders. B handles setup well by having the seller do it, but it gives no wording for replying to a prospect and its qualification advice is thinner. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers take a clear conditional position and deal directly with the day of setup, offering assisted setup or a pilot on one team. B does better on qualification: it gives four concrete gate questions, and its pilot terms include a success test, a named signer and a booked decision meeting. B also gives a reply to send the prospect, while A only gives wording for the cofounder and advice on what to ask.
